Raw results and interpretation are durable under bench/forwarding/results. Final default build/CTest 1/1, pure route tests, git diff check, and unchanged live X topology passed.

handoffs.note: Implemented PCI-identity-resolved transport benchmark harness with exact-byte validation, 5 warmups, 7 trials, 5 sizes (4 KiB to 256 MiB), JSONL output, and CUDA-controller campaign specs. Accepted uncontaminated evidence d1c4849c-5bbc-4b85-954b-733d26301bfb: at 256 MiB direct NV6 SM-pull averaged 136.88 GB/s (136.85-136.89), same-NUMA PHB P2P averaged 5.18 GB/s (5.15-5.21), and current non-P2P SYS CUDA fallback averaged 5.81 GB/s (5.74-5.87). All 60 direction/size correctness cases passed. Raw results and summary preserved. NVIDIA simpleP2P independently passed 64 MiB A0/A1 correctness and 131.88 GB/s (evidence a90f3c84-e3bc-4920-a37b-5219f5f8499d). An early invalid harness attempt caused one Xid 31 due incorrect transfer ordering; it was rejected, corrected, and no new Xid occurred. No reset/topology change performed. nvcc warnings clean aside from deprecated pre-sm75 offline support notice; JSON count validation and git diff --check passed.

invariants.rule: Performance claims require recorded topology, software versions, baselines, and before/after measurements; serious profiling uses the installed CUDA skill.
Do not implement or optimize a custom forwarding primitive before topology, transport baselines, and stock NCCL behavior provide measured evidence.

Keep numaBraid specific to the present CUDA, NCCL, GPU P2P, NVLink, PCIe, dual-NUMA four-GPU X topology; do not introduce generic fabric, endpoint, router, FPGA, or hypothetical-hardware abstractions.
Measure and characterize stock NCCL before implementing a custom relay; use NCCL when it already provides the required semantics near physical-link speed.

For an optimized forwarding path with an available local-GPU to NVLink route, payload data must not traverse the CPU inter-socket link; fallbacks must be explicit and must not masquerade as optimized.

tasks.objective: Establish the compact repository, authoritative documentation, C++20 build skeleton, header compile smoke coverage, optional public module boundary, and todo-orchestrator foundation without implementing forwarding.
tasks.title: Repository bootstrap

tasks.notes: Do not infer physical identity from CUDA ordinals. Validate PCI, NUMA, CUDA peer, and NVLink relationships at runtime.
tasks.objective: Implement a small explicit probe for CUDA GPUs, PCI identities, NUMA locality, CUDA peer access, NVLink pairs, and the carrier relationships required by numaBraid, without building a generic graph framework.
tasks.title: Discover and validate X topology

tasks.notes: Record topology and software versions. Keep hardware benchmarks separate from ordinary compile/unit tests.
tasks.objective: Build the minimal benchmark harness for local PCIe P2P, direct NVLink, cross-NUMA baseline, and relevant NCCL paths across transfer sizes and directions.
tasks.title: Establish transport benchmark harness

tasks.notes: Do not assume a custom relay is needed and do not replace NCCL without evidence.
tasks.objective: Determine and measure how installed NCCL handles the X topology, including any intermediate-GPU or NVB-like forwarding, and answer whether it avoids host inter-socket payload traversal near bottleneck throughput.
tasks.title: Characterize stock NCCL forwarding

tasks.notes: Headers remain default. Modules remain opt-in, public-boundary-only, and must not force CUDA or downstream module adoption.
tasks.objective: Refine the small header-first public boundary, optional module interface, library target, and consumer build integration without designing a forwarding API.
tasks.title: Stabilize minimal public integration boundary

tasks.notes: Set the forwarding-strategy decision only from measured evidence. Downstream custom implementation remains inactive unless the value is custom-relay.
tasks.objective: Use measured topology, transport, and NCCL evidence to select stock NCCL, narrow NCCL specialization, or a dedicated numaBraid relay.
tasks.title: Forwarding strategy decision

tasks.objective: If and only if evidence selects a custom relay, implement the narrow X-path forwarding primitive for maximum throughput.
tasks.title: Implement custom forwarding primitive

tasks.objective: Empirically tune chunking, staging, overlap, streams, events, and synchronization toward steady-state bottleneck-link throughput.
tasks.title: Pipeline and tune forwarding

tasks.objective: Measure explicit NUMA-controlled host-staged GPU diagonals, isolated host inter-socket movement, and comparable numaBraid relay behavior through 12 GiB under single-flow and concurrent load without changing relay tuning or physical topology.
tasks.title: Characterize large host-inter-socket transport
